correctness.rationale: For each positive integer branch count, the basis consisting of edge-supported x and x² and the shared hub lift q=1-4x+(10/3)x² is orthogonal, with per-edge q²-integral 1/9. Inverting the 2x2 monomial Gram block gives the exact reproducing kernel K0 plus 9q(x)q(y)/k. At a leaf the same-edge kernel is an explicit upward quadratic with two interior roots and discriminant 24(t²+2t+6); other edges have kernel 3tq. The exact L1 integral produces E_k and, by sign data, is an attained evaluation norm. The derivative factor (t-1)(t+6) proves monotonicity; symbolic limits establish both saturation constants; exact radical comparison proves the threshold k>=3. Reproduction of the constant one gives negative kernel mass (E_k-1)/2 and its 0<=f<=1 extremizer. The delivered Python/SymPy checker rederives exact identities and 291 independent Gram/kernel/root checks. No full global projector norm is claimed.

value.rationale: The sharp boundary evaluation functional is a natural invariant of least-squares reconstruction on branching metric domains, while its negative kernel mass gives an exact and attained positivity-loss phenomenon. The formula covers every arm count, proves strict amplification with branching, determines the first crossing of 5/2 at three arms, and computes both the limiting strength and first-order saturation rate. These structural changes cannot be inferred from interval general boundedness or linear-degree graph estimates and are useful for choosing approximation spaces at branch junctions.
